problem:
A delivery pod of mass $28\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the pod is proportional to its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=7\,\text{kg/s}$ and acts opposite to the direction of motion.

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the pod? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the pod are the weight due to gravity and drag.

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $12\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the body is proportional to its velocity and acts in the opposite direction to the motion.
At a particular moment during the fall, the body’s velocity is $10\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $6.3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the body? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the body are the weight due to gravity and drag.

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Terminal velocity is the constant speed a falling object approaches as the upward resistive force (drag) grows to exactly balance the downward gravitational force.
That is, at terminal velocity (a constant), acceleration is zero, so by $F=ma,$ the resultant force is zero.

First, note that only two forces act on the body: the force due to gravity, given by the weight

$$
w=mg=12\cdot 9.8=117.6\,\text{N},
$$

and the force due to drag $D,$ which is proportional to the velocity (and negative since it acts in the negative direction),

$$
D=-kv,
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality. Hence, the resultant force acting on the body is

$$
F=w+D=117.6-kv.
$$

Applying Newton's second law, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\ 117.6-kv & =12a\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that, at a particular moment, the body’s velocity is $10\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $6.3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ Substituting these values into the above, we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}117.6-10k & =12\cdot 6.3 \\ 117.6-10k & =75.6 \\ -10k & =-42 \\ k & =4.2\,\text{kg/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the resultant force acting on the body is

$$
F=117.6-4.2v.
$$

When the body reaches terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}},$ the resultant force is zero:

$$
117.6-4.2{v}_{\text{term}}=0\,⟹\,{v}_{\text{term}}=\frac{117.6}{4.2}=28
$$

Therefore, the terminal velocity of the body is ${v}_{\text{term}}=28\,\text{m/s}.$
